Hot-spot threshold of the Short-D'Orsogna-Brantingham model

Source: R/sdb.R
sdbthr.Rd

The continuum model of sdbsim() has one uniform steady state, \(\bar b = \epsilon D \gamma / \omega\), \(\bar A = a_0 + \bar b\), \(\bar\rho = \gamma / \bar A\). Linearised about it, a disturbance of wavenumber-squared \(k\) evolves by a 2 by 2 matrix whose trace is negative at every \(k\) and whose determinant is \(P k^2 - Q k + R\), \(R = \omega \bar A > 0\): a mode grows exactly when the determinant is negative. So hot spots form when \(Q > 0\), that is \(3 \epsilon D \bar\rho > \omega + \eta \bar A\) (repeat victimisation outweighs decay and spreading), and \(Q^2 > 4 P R\); the fastest-growing mode is near \(k^* = Q / (2 P)\). Without reinforcement (eps = 0) the uniform state is stable at every wavelength (proof("sdbthr")). z places the lattice's neighbour count on both diffusion terms, as sdbsim() does (z = 1 is the continuum form).

Usage

sdbthr(a0, omega, eps, dif, gam, eta, z = 1, k = NULL)

Arguments

a0, omega, eps, dif, gam, eta, z

The model's constants, as for sdbsim(): one number each, eps and eta from 0, the others positive.

k

NULL or wavenumbers-squared (numbers from 0) at which to tabulate the trace, the determinant and the growth rate.

Value

An object of class sdbthr, a list: steady (b, a, rho); p, q, r, the determinant's coefficients; thr, the two sides of the threshold (lhs \(3 \epsilon D \bar\rho\), rhs \(\omega + \eta \bar A\)); unstable; kcrit, detcrit, grcrit, the critical mode, its determinant and growth rate (NA unless p and q are positive); and disp, NULL or a data frame (k, trace, det, growth).

References

Short, M. B., Bertozzi, A. L. and Brantingham, P. J. (2010). Nonlinear patterns in urban crime: hotspots, bifurcations, and suppression. SIAM Journal on Applied Dynamical Systems, 9(2), 462-483. doi:10.1137/090759069

Examples

sdbthr(a0 = 1, omega = 1, eps = 2, dif = 1, gam = 1, eta = 0.01)
#> sdbthr: steady b 2, rho 0.3333333; 3 eps dif rho = 2 against omega + eta A = 1.03
#> hot spots form; critical k 48.5
sdbthr(a0 = 1, omega = 1, eps = 0, dif = 1, gam = 1, eta = 0.01)$unstable
#> [1] FALSE
